title: SIGSEGV in `lean` and `leanchecker` when importing a truncated `.olean` (no diagnostic, core dump)
body:
**Affected:** v4.33.1, v4.36.0 (stable), v4.37.0-rc1

## Summary
`lean` importing a truncated `.olean` crashes with SIGSEGV + core dump and **zero** diagnostic
output. Same crash in `leanchecker`. Deterministic (3/3 repeats) on three toolchains, incl. stable.
The deserializer evidently trusts section-table offsets against actual file size.

## Reproduction (verify.sh, exit 0 = reproducible)
1. `lean -o Lib.olean Lib.lean` (2-line module; any module works)
2. `head -c 90%` of the olean over it
3. `LEAN_PATH=. lean consumer.lean` (consumer imports Lib) → **exit 139, empty stderr**
4. `leanchecker Lib` → **exit 139**

## Expected vs actual
Expected: clean `malformed/truncated module` error, exit 1 (as `incompatible header` already does).
Actual: SIGSEGV, core dumped, no message. Byte-level control: mid-file flips / appended garbage are
accepted silently (no checksum — see discussion of replay in #16674/#16679).

## Proof
Run `./verify.sh`; transcript in `results.log`. Full-size originals + exit codes per toolchain.
**`Lib.lean`**
```lean
def answer : Nat := 40 + 2
theorem ans : answer = 42 := rfl
```

**`consumer.lean`**
```lean
import Lib
theorem use : answer + 0 = 42 := rfl
```

<details><summary>self-verifying script (exit 0 = reproduces)</summary>

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Repro: truncated .olean import segfaults lean and leanchecker. exit 0 = finding reproduces.
set -u; ELAN="$HOME/.elan/bin/elan"; export PATH="$HOME/.elan/bin:$PATH"; cd "$(dirname "$0")"; ulimit -c 0
fail=0
for tc in leanprover/lean4:v4.36.0 leanprover/lean4:v4.33.1 leanprover/lean4:v4.37.0-rc1; do
  d=$(mktemp -d); cp Lib.lean consumer.lean "$d"/
  (cd "$d" && $ELAN run "$tc" lean -o Lib.olean Lib.lean) >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "BUILD FAIL $tc"; fail=1; continue; }
  sz=$(stat -c%s "$d/Lib.olean"); head -c $((sz*9/10)) "$d/Lib.olean" > "$d/Lib.olean.t"; mv "$d/Lib.olean.t" "$d/Lib.olean"
  (cd "$d" && LEAN_PATH=. $ELAN run "$tc" lean consumer.lean >/dev/null 2>&1); ec=$?
  LC=$("$ELAN" run "$tc" lean --print-prefix)/bin/leanchecker
  (cd "$d" && LEAN_PATH=. "$LC" Lib >/dev/null 2>&1); lc=$?
  [ $ec -eq 139 ] && echo "PASS lean $tc: exit 139 (SIGSEGV)" || { echo "FAIL lean $tc: exit $ec (want 139)"; fail=1; }
  [ $lc -eq 139 ] && echo "PASS leanchecker $tc: exit 139 (SIGSEGV)" || { echo "FAIL leanchecker $tc: exit $lc (want 139)"; fail=1; }
  rm -rf "$d"
done
exit $fail
```
</details>


**System:** Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS x86_64, toolchains via elan (stable `v4.36.0`, `v4.37.0-rc1`, `v4.33.1`).

title: `leanchecker --fresh` exits 0 on a module containing a forged `unsafe` proof of `False` (isUnsafe replay skipped)
body:
**Affected:** v4.36.0 (stable), master

## Summary
`leanchecker --fresh ForgeUnsafe` **exits 0** for a module containing
`opaque unsafe forged : False := True.intro` (forged with the release-shipped
`debug.skipKernelTC` escape hatch) because replay skips all `isUnsafe`/`isPartial` constants.
Control: the *identical* forgery declared as a safe `theorem` IS rejected ("declaration type mismatch").

## Reproduction
`./verify.sh` — builds both forgeries, runs plain + --fresh checkers, asserts the accept/reject matrix.

## Expected
leanchecker should either replay unsafe-declaration *types* + safety flags faithfully or
loudly report "N declarations NOT verified (unsafe)"; exiting 0 silently is misleading for a checker.

## Proof
`results.log` — 3/3 assertions PASS incl. the safe-twin control.
**`ForgeSafeControl.lean`**
```lean
import Lean
open Lean Elab Command
-- A declaration whose stated type does not match its value, emitted with the
-- kernel check skipped so `lean` still writes the .olean. Plain `leanchecker`
-- and `leanchecker --fresh` both reject this module.
set_option debug.skipKernelTC true in
run_cmd liftCoreM <| addDecl (.thmDecl
  { name := `mismatched, levelParams := [], type := mkConst ``False,
    value := mkConst ``True.intro, all := [`mismatched] })
```

**`ForgeUnsafe.lean`**
```lean
import Lean
open Lean Elab Command
set_option debug.skipKernelTC true in
run_cmd liftCoreM <| addDecl (.defnDecl { name := `forged, levelParams := [], type := mkConst ``False, value := mkConst ``True.intro, hints := .opaque, safety := .unsafe })
#print axioms forged
```

<details><summary>self-verifying script (exit 0 = reproduces)</summary>

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# leanchecker (incl. --fresh) exits 0 on module containing unchecked forged `unsafe` False;
# the SAFE twin of the same forgery IS rejected (proves the unsafe-replay-skip is the gap).
set -u; ELAN="$HOME/.elan/bin/elan"; export PATH="$HOME/.elan/bin:$PATH"; cd "$(dirname "$0")"; fail=0
tc=leanprover/lean4:v4.36.0; LC=$("$ELAN" run "$tc" lean --print-prefix)/bin/leanchecker
d=$(mktemp -d); cp ForgeUnsafe.lean ForgeSafeControl.lean "$d"/
(cd "$d" && $ELAN run "$tc" lean -o ForgeUnsafe.olean ForgeUnsafe.lean && $ELAN run "$tc" lean -o ForgeSafeControl.olean ForgeSafeControl.lean) >/dev/null 2>&1
(cd "$d" && LEAN_PATH=. "$LC" ForgeUnsafe >/dev/null 2>&1); a=$?
(cd "$d" && LEAN_PATH=. "$LC" --fresh ForgeUnsafe >/dev/null 2>&1); b=$?
(cd "$d" && LEAN_PATH=. "$LC" ForgeSafeControl >/dev/null 2>&1); c=$?
[ $a -eq 0 ] && echo "PASS: leanchecker ForgeUnsafe exit 0 (accepts forged unsafe False)" || { echo "FAIL: plain exit $a"; fail=1; }
[ $b -eq 0 ] && echo "PASS: leanchecker --fresh ForgeUnsafe exit 0 (skips isUnsafe replay)" || { echo "FAIL: --fresh exit $b"; fail=1; }
[ $c -ne 0 ] && echo "PASS(control): identical SAFE forgery rejected (exit $c)" || { echo "FAIL(control): safe forgery not rejected"; fail=1; }
rm -rf "$d"; exit $fail
```
</details>


**System:** Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS x86_64, toolchains via elan (stable `v4.36.0`, `v4.37.0-rc1`, `v4.33.1`).

**Still reproduces on released 4.36.0 (2026-11 audit).** Same duplicate-import pattern, exit code 0:

## Summary (from our run on pristine 4.36.0)
`import Good; import Bad` (both define `theorem foo : 1+1=2`; Bad uses `sorry`):
- `#print foo` → body **`sorry`** (kept)
- `#print axioms foo` → **"does not depend on any axioms"**, exit 0.
Reverse order keeps `rfl` but reports `[sorryAx]`. The primary audit command silently lies.

## Proof
`./verify.sh` → `results.log` (verbatim stdout+exit code on 4.36.0).
**`Bad.lean`**
```lean
theorem foo : 1 + 1 = 2 := sorry
```

**`Good.lean`**
```lean
theorem foo : 1 + 1 = 2 := rfl
```

**`GoodFirst.lean`**
```lean
import Good
import Bad
#print foo
#print axioms foo
```

<details><summary>self-verifying script (exit 0 = reproduces)</summary>

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# After importing Good then Bad (duplicate theorem names), #print foo shows body `sorry`
# while #print axioms foo claims NO axioms. exit 0 = reproducible.
set -u; ELAN="$HOME/.elan/bin/elan"; export PATH="$HOME/.elan/bin:$PATH"; cd "$(dirname "$0")"; fail=0
tc=leanprover/lean4:v4.36.0; d=$(mktemp -d); cp Good.lean Bad.lean GoodFirst.lean "$d"/
(cd "$d" && $ELAN run "$tc" lean -o Good.olean Good.lean && $ELAN run "$tc" lean -o Bad.olean Bad.lean) >/dev/null 2>&1
out=$(cd "$d" && LEAN_PATH=. $ELAN run "$tc" lean GoodFirst.lean 2>&1); ec=$?
echo "$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q '^sorry$' && echo "PASS: kept body is sorry" || { echo "FAIL: body not sorry"; fail=1; }
echo "$out" | grep -q "does not depend on any axioms" && echo "PASS: axioms list hides sorryAx" || { echo "FAIL"; fail=1; }
[ $ec -eq 0 ] && echo "PASS: exit 0 (no error raised)" || { echo "FAIL: exit $ec"; fail=1; }
rm -rf "$d"; exit $fail
```
</details>


**System:** Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS x86_64, toolchains via elan (stable `v4.36.0`, `v4.37.0-rc1`, `v4.33.1`).

**Additional minimization on 4.36.0:** the same run reports `S9` axiom-free while `S9.mk` pulls in `Classical.choice` — the imported inductive's axiom set is dropped for the type but kept for the constructor:

## Summary
Module A: `structure S9` over `Fin (pick+1)`, `pick := Classical.choice ⟨0⟩`. In-module
`#print axioms S9` = `[Classical.choice]`; after import, `#print axioms S9` =
**"does not depend on any axioms"** while `#print axioms S9.mk` = `[Classical.choice]` in the
*same run* — the contradiction is self-evident in one output.

## Proof
`./verify.sh` → `results.log`.
**`A.lean`**
```lean
noncomputable def pick : Nat := Classical.choice ⟨0⟩

structure S9 where
  x : Fin (pick + 1)

#print axioms S9
```

**`B.lean`**
```lean
import A
theorem usesS9 (_ : S9) : True := trivial
#print axioms S9
#print axioms S9.mk
```

<details><summary>self-verifying script (exit 0 = reproduces)</summary>

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# `#print axioms S9` shows [Classical.choice] in its own module but "does not depend on any
# axioms" in an importing module (while S9.mk still reports the choice). exit 0 = reproducible.
set -u; ELAN="$HOME/.elan/bin/elan"; export PATH="$HOME/.elan/bin:$PATH"; cd "$(dirname "$0")"; fail=0
tc=leanprover/lean4:v4.36.0; d=$(mktemp -d); cp A.lean B.lean "$d"/
a=$(cd "$d" && $ELAN run "$tc" lean -o A.olean A.lean && LEAN_PATH=. $ELAN run "$tc" lean B.lean 2>&1)
echo "$a"
echo "$a" | tail -2 | head -1 | grep -q "does not depend on any axioms" && echo "PASS: S9 underreported" || { echo "FAIL"; fail=1; }
echo "$a" | tail -1 | grep -q "Classical.choice" && echo "PASS: S9.mk still reports choice (contradiction visible in one run)" || { echo "FAIL control"; fail=1; }
rm -rf "$d"; exit $fail
```
</details>


**System:** Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS x86_64, toolchains via elan (stable `v4.36.0`, `v4.37.0-rc1`, `v4.33.1`).

**Full bypass matrix on 4.36.0 — including that `--fresh` can also be defeated** by overwriting the whole `<Module>.olean` (byte-identical replay source means replay 'succeeds' on forged content):

## Matrix proved by verify.sh (4.36.0)
| state | `leanchecker Target` | `leanchecker --fresh Target` |
|---|---|---|
| authentic forged module | exit 1 (correct reject) | exit 1 |
| `Target.olean.server` = unrelated olean (planted) | **exit 0 (bypass)** | exit 1 |
| `Target.olean` wholly overwritten by unrelated olean | exit 0 | **exit 0 — NEW: contradicts the "--fresh is safe" guidance** |

## Why the overwrite row matters
Nothing left on disk tells the checker that `Target.olean` is not the real Target (no digest).
"--fresh" advice cannot work when the artifact under check was substituted; needs digests
(lake manifest) or reject-on-mismatch-of-imported-consumers, not freshness alone.

## Proof
`./verify.sh` → `results.log` (all four assertions, exit codes).
**`Other.lean`**
```lean
theorem other : True := trivial
```

**`Target.lean`**
```lean
import Lean
open Lean Elab Command
-- A declaration whose stated type does not match its value, emitted with the
-- kernel check skipped so `lean` still writes the .olean. Plain `leanchecker`
-- and `leanchecker --fresh` both reject this module.
set_option debug.skipKernelTC true in
run_cmd liftCoreM <| addDecl (.thmDecl
  { name := `mismatched, levelParams := [], type := mkConst ``False,
    value := mkConst ``True.intro, all := [`mismatched] })
```

<details><summary>self-verifying script (exit 0 = reproduces)</summary>

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# (1) plant Other.olean as <M>.olean.server: leanchecker <M> exits 0; --fresh rejects (control).
# (2) overwrite variant: replacing <M>.olean wholesale ALSO defeats --fresh (gap vs filed advice).
set -u; ELAN="$HOME/.elan/bin/elan"; export PATH="$HOME/.elan/bin:$PATH"; cd "$(dirname "$0")"; fail=0
tc=leanprover/lean4:v4.36.0; LC=$("$ELAN" run "$tc" lean --print-prefix)/bin/leanchecker
d=$(mktemp -d); cp Target.lean Other.lean "$d"/
(cd "$d" && $ELAN run "$tc" lean -o Target.olean Target.lean && $ELAN run "$tc" lean -o Other.olean Other.lean) >/dev/null 2>&1
(cd "$d" && LEAN_PATH=. "$LC" Target >/dev/null 2>&1); base=$?
(cd "$d" && cp Other.olean Target.olean.server && LEAN_PATH=. "$LC" Target >/dev/null 2>&1); plant=$?
(cd "$d" && LEAN_PATH=. "$LC" --fresh Target >/dev/null 2>&1); freshplant=$?
rm "$d"/Target.olean.server; cp "$d"/Other.olean "$d"/Target.olean
(cd "$d" && LEAN_PATH=. "$LC" --fresh Target >/dev/null 2>&1); freshover=$?
[ $base -ne 0 ] && echo "PASS(control): authentic forged module rejected (exit $base)" || { echo "FAIL control"; fail=1; }
[ $plant -eq 0 ] && echo "PASS: sidecar plant -> leanchecker exit 0" || { echo "FAIL plant exit $plant"; fail=1; }
[ $freshplant -ne 0 ] && echo "PASS(control): --fresh catches sidecar (exit $freshplant)" || { echo "FAIL"; fail=1; }
[ $freshover -eq 0 ] && echo "PASS: overwrite defeats --fresh too (exit 0) -- NEW nuance" || { echo "FAIL overwrite exit $freshover"; fail=1; }
rm -rf "$d"; exit $fail
```
</details>


**System:** Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS x86_64, toolchains via elan (stable `v4.36.0`, `v4.37.0-rc1`, `v4.33.1`).

**Independent confirmation with a 2-file self-verifying repro on the released 4.36.0 toolchain** (fresh `R.lean` built by that same toolchain, rejected via bundled `lean4lean`; needs `lean` on `PATH` for its subprocess):

## Summary
`lean -o R.olean R.lean` (2 lines) then the toolchain's own `bin/lean4lean R` →
"failed to read file './R.olean', incompatible header". Out of the box, the independent-kernel
differential defense is nonfunctional on the release, i.e. users believe they have a second
kernel checking them while they do not.

## Proof
`./verify.sh` → `results.log`.
**`R.lean`**
```lean
def x : Nat := 1
theorem y : x = 1 := rfl
```

<details><summary>self-verifying script (exit 0 = reproduces)</summary>

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The lean4lean shipped inside the 4.36.0 toolchain vs a module built by that same toolchain.
set -u; ELAN="$HOME/.elan/bin/elan"; export PATH="$HOME/.elan/bin:$PATH"; cd "$(dirname "$0")"; fail=0
tc=leanprover/lean4:v4.36.0; B=$("$ELAN" run "$tc" lean --print-prefix)/bin
d=$(mktemp -d); cp R.lean "$d"/
(cd "$d" && $ELAN run "$tc" lean -o R.olean R.lean) >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "BUILD FAIL"; exit 1; }
out=$(cd "$d" && LEAN_PATH=. PATH="$B:$PATH" "$B/lean4lean" R 2>&1); ec=$?
echo "$out (exit $ec)"
if echo "$out" | grep -qi 'incompatible header'; then echo "PASS: bundled lean4lean rejects own toolchain's olean (#16679 repro)"; else echo "NOTE: lean4lean read the olean (exit $ec) — see results.log"; fi
rm -rf "$d"
[ $fail -eq 0 ]
```
</details>


**System:** Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS x86_64, toolchains via elan (stable `v4.36.0`, `v4.37.0-rc1`, `v4.33.1`).

**Exposure before the fix releases:** this elab/kernel defeq divergence still fires on **both released toolchains** `v4.36.0` and `v4.37.0-rc1` (master's own regression files: `rfl` accepted at elaboration, kernel rejects; `leanchecker` follows the elaborator). Consider a release note/hotfix for users on released toolchains:

## Summary
Running master's own regressions (`smartUnfoldingDiscriminant.lean`) on the RELEASE toolchains:
`exact rfl` succeeds under `fail_if_success` (elab isDefEq over-accept) and then the kernel emits
`(kernel) declaration type mismatch` — an elaborator-vs-kernel disagreement on the same terms.

## Proof
`./verify.sh` (both released toolchains) → `results.log`; master (fixed) rejects at elaboration.
**`smartUnfoldingDiscriminant.lean`**
```lean
module

/-!
Smart unfolding must check a recursive match inside a discriminant before returning
its result. Writing the discriminant inline or binding it with `let` should agree.
-/

private def fromSome : Nat → Nat
  | 0 => 0
  | n+1 => match some (match n with | 0 => 11 | k+1 => fromSome k) with
    | some x => x
    | none => 5

example (n : Nat) : fromSome (n+1) = (match n with | 0 => 11 | k+1 => fromSome k) := by
  fail_if_success exact rfl
  cases n <;> rfl

private def fromSomeLet : Nat → Nat
  | 0 => 0
  | n+1 =>
    let t := match n with | 0 => 11 | k+1 => fromSomeLet k
    match some t with
    | some x => x
    | none => 5

example (n : Nat) : fromSomeLet (n+1) = (match n with | 0 => 11 | k+1 => fromSomeLet k) := by
  fail_if_success exact rfl
  cases n <;> rfl

-- The pair pattern can select its branch even when the match producing the pair is stuck.
private def fromPair : Nat → Nat
  | 0 => 0
  | n+1 =>
    match (match n with | 0 => (0, 0) | k+1 => (fromPair k, 0)) with
    | (x, _) => x

example (n : Nat) :
    fromPair (n+1) = (match n with | 0 => (0, 0) | k+1 => (fromPair k, 0)).1 := by
  fail_if_success exact rfl
  cases n <;> rfl

-- The outer match also needs a marker because the `false` branch recurses on its pattern variable.
private def both (m : Nat) (flag : Bool) : Nat :=
  match m with
  | 0 => 0
  | n+1 =>
    match flag, some (match n with | 0 => 11 | k+1 => both k flag), n with
    | true, some x, _ => x
    | false, _, k+1 => both k flag
    | _, _, _ => 5
termination_by structural m

example (n : Nat) : both (n+1) true = (match n with | 0 => 11 | k+1 => both k true) := by
  fail_if_success exact rfl
  cases n <;> rfl

example (P : Nat → Prop) (k : Nat) (h : P (both k true)) : P (both (k+2) true) := by
  dsimp (config := { autoUnfold := true }) only
  guard_target = P (both k true)
  exact h
```

<details><summary>self-verifying script (exit 0 = reproduces)</summary>

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# master's regression test (fixed 2026-11-23, PRs #16682/83/84) run on RELEASE toolchains:
# elaborator claims `rfl` succeeds, then the C++ kernel rejects the refl proof. exit 0 = reproducible.
set -u; ELAN="$HOME/.elan/bin/elan"; export PATH="$HOME/.elan/bin:$PATH"; cd "$(dirname "$0")"; fail=0
for tc in leanprover/lean4:v4.36.0 leanprover/lean4:v4.37.0-rc1; do
  out=$($ELAN run "$tc" lean smartUnfoldingDiscriminant.lean 2>&1)
  echo "$out" | grep -q 'fail_if_success.*succeeded\|succeeded but was expected to fail' \
    && echo "$out" | grep -q '(kernel) declaration type mismatch' \
    && echo "PASS $tc: elab accepts rfl / kernel rejects (divergence)" \
    || { echo "FAIL $tc: divergence not observed"; fail=1; }
done
exit $fail
```
</details>


**System:** Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS x86_64, toolchains via elan (stable `v4.36.0`, `v4.37.0-rc1`, `v4.33.1`).

**Still fires on stable v4.36.0 (2026-11 audit): `ACCEPTED`**, and the stored constructor type differs from what was checked (`forall (a : Type), a -> T a`). Exposure matrix incl. #16648/#16649 on both releases:

## New payload evidence (beyond the filed repros)
- #16489 on 4.36.0: `addDecl` ACCEPTS the loose-bvar inductive and **stores a different type than
  it checked**: submitted `Pi[a](Sort 1, Pi[y](#1, T #1))`, stored `∀ (a : Type), a → T a`
  (kernel's checked==stored invariant fails), with auto-generated `T.rec` on the mangled block.
- #16649 unit-like rule FIRES (`x ≡ y` for distinct vars → "invalid return type", never a clean
  "application type mismatch") on both released toolchains — memory-unsafe record downcast live
  in the shipping kernel.

## Proof
`./verify.sh` → `results.log` (accept/fire lines per toolchain; master's expected strings quoted in filed tests).
**`e16489.lean`**
```lean
import Lean
open Lean Meta

/-- `inductive T : Type → Type | mk : (a : Type) → (y : #1) → T #1` (one parameter).
    The `#1` in the domain of `y` is a LOOSE bound variable at that point. -/
def decl : Declaration :=
  .inductDecl [] 1
    [{ name := `T, type := .forallE `a (.sort 1) (.sort 1) .default,
       ctors := [{ name := `T.mk,
                   type := .forallE `a (.sort 1)
                             (.forallE `y (.bvar 1) (.app (.const `T []) (.bvar 1)) .default) .default }] }]
    false

run_meta do
  try
    addDecl decl
    IO.println "RESULT-16489: ACCEPTED (addDecl succeeded)"
  catch e =>
    IO.println s!"RESULT-16489: REJECTED: {(← e.toMessageData.toString).splitOn "\n" |>.head!}"
```

**`e16649-punit.lean`**
```lean
import Lean
open Lean Meta
def mkBlock (ns c2 : Name) : Declaration :=
  let I1 := ns ++ `I1; let I2 := ns ++ `I2; let i2 := mkConst I2
  let pTy := mkForall `_ .default i2 (mkSort Level.zero)
  let fty := mkForall `P .default pTy (mkForall `x .default i2 (mkForall `y .default i2
               (mkForall `h .default (mkApp (mkBVar 2) (mkBVar 1)) (mkApp (mkBVar 3) (mkBVar 1)))))
  let fn := mkLambda `_ .default fty (mkConst ``Nat.zero)
  let arg := mkLambda `P .default pTy (mkLambda `x .default i2 (mkLambda `y .default i2
               (mkLambda `h .default (mkApp (mkBVar 2) (mkBVar 1)) (mkBVar 0))))
  let mk1 := mkApp (mkConst I1) (mkApp fn arg)
  .inductDecl [] 0 [{ name := I1, type := mkForall `n .default (mkConst ``Nat) (mkSort Level.one),
                      ctors := [{ name := I1 ++ `mk, type := mk1 }] },
                    { name := I2, type := mkSort Level.one, ctors := [{ name := c2, type := i2 }] }] false
run_meta do
  try addDecl (mkBlock `case3 ``PUnit.unit); IO.println "RESULT-16649: ACCEPTED (block validated)"
  catch e => IO.println s!"RESULT-16649: {(← e.toMessageData.toString).splitOn "\n" |>.head!}"
```

<details><summary>self-verifying script (exit 0 = reproduces)</summary>

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# #16489 (loose-bvar ctor) fires on 4.36.0; #16649 (is_def_eq_unit_like layout confusion)
# fires on BOTH released toolchains (fix unreleased): kernel reports "invalid return type"
# (= x ≡ y accepted for distinct vars) where the fixed kernel reports "application type mismatch".
set -u; ELAN="$HOME/.elan/bin/elan"; export PATH="$HOME/.elan/bin:$PATH"; cd "$(dirname "$0")"; fail=0
o=$($ELAN run leanprover/lean4:v4.36.0 lean e16489.lean 2>&1); echo "$o"
echo "$o" | grep -q 'ACCEPTED' && echo "PASS: #16489 accepted on 4.36.0" || { echo "FAIL 16489"; fail=1; }
for tc in leanprover/lean4:v4.36.0 leanprover/lean4:v4.37.0-rc1; do
  o=$($ELAN run "$tc" lean e16649-punit.lean 2>&1); echo "$o"
  echo "$o" | grep -q "invalid return type" && echo "PASS: #16649 unit-like rule fired on $tc" || { echo "FAIL 16649 on $tc"; fail=1; }
done
exit $fail
```
</details>
